lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: revealing zeros, extrema, and growth rate from algebraic form
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: revealing zeros, extrema, and growth rate from algebraic form

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Function f is given in vertex form as f(x) = −(x + 3)² − 5, so it opens downward. Function g is given by a table whose greatest output is -1. Which function has the greater maximum, and by how much?
The function f(x) = (x − 4)² + 4 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.
A polynomial has degree 5 and leading coefficient -5. Describe its end behaviour.
choices: the left end falls and the right end rises
the left end rises and the right end falls

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: For f(x) = (x + 3) / (x + 5), state the vertical asymptote and the horizontal asymptote.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Function f is given in vertex form as f(x) = −(x − 2)² + 4, so it opens downward. Function g is given by a table whose greatest output is 8. Which function has the greater maximum, and by how much?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: The function f(x) = 2(x + 3)² − 10 opens upward. State its minimum value and where it occurs.
